title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the 1975–76 divided-power de Rham notes. It is a typescript page (Exposé IX, p. 108), photographed upside down and evidently reused as scrap paper. The text is from SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §9.3 on 'extensions panachées' (multiple extensions).

Setting: an abelian category with fixed objects P, Q, R. E and F are extensions sharing a middle term. A panached extension X of E by F is an object with a 3-step filtration whose two-step pieces realise E and F. These form a category EXTPAN(E,F).

Known structure (9.3.x):
- EXTPAN(E,F) is nonempty iff the Yoneda product of E and F vanishes in Ext^2.
- When nonempty, EXTPAN(E,F) is a torsor under the Picard category EXT(Q,P), acting by Baer-sum-type operations (H, X) ↦ H∧X. The action satisfies an associativity formula (9.3.7).
- ω is a comparison arrow (9.3.5).

On this page an exact functor r : C → C' is applied. It transports everything to E' = r(E), F' = r(F), P' = r(P), Q' = r(Q). The compatibility diagram (from the preceding page) is used as follows:
1. Fix X in EXTPAN(E,F) and set X' = r(X).
2. The functor G' ↦ G'∧X' gives an equivalence EXT(Q',P') ≅ EXTPAN(E',F').
3. Hence any Y' in EXTPAN(E',F') is determined up to isomorphism by a class c_X(Y') ∈ Ext^1(Q',P').
4. Replacing X by X_1 = H∧X, with H ∈ EXT(Q,P), shifts the class: c_{X_1}(Y') = c_X(Y') − cl(H'), where H' = r(H), by associativity.
5. So the image c(Y') ∈ Ext^1(Q',P') / Im Ext^1(Q,P) is canonical (9.3.13).
6. c(Y') = 0 iff Y' is isomorphic to r of some panached extension of E by F. In other words, it is the obstruction to descending a panached extension along r.

In SGA 7 this serves the study of the monodromy pairing and of the descent of extensions along change of base (e.g. passing to the generic fibre or to the strict henselisation).
errors: The displayed formula reads c_{X_1}(Y') = c_X(Y) − cl(H'); the right side should be c_X(Y'). This is a typographical slip, either in the typescript or in the transcription.
The sign in front of cl(H') depends on the conventions for the action; this is immaterial for the quotient class.

ideas.what: Panached (multiple) extensions as a torsor under EXT(Q,P), with an obstruction class modulo the image of Ext^1(Q,P) for descending a panached extension along an exact functor
ideas.modern_name: Torsor structure on 2-step (Massey-type) extensions; relative obstruction class / extension of scalars for blended extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 I Exposé IX §9.3 (1967–69, publ. 1972)
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, §9.3 (Lecture Notes in Math. 288)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX typescript, reused as scrap paper and photographed upside down. Its content is published verbatim and well known; it has nothing to do with the divided-power de Rham notes.
transcription_corrections: The image is upside down; the page is typescript SGA 7 Exposé IX p. 108, archive number 426, not a handwritten note.
In the formula 'c_{X_1}(Y') = c_X(Y) - cl(H')', the right side should be c_X(Y'), and the subscript in the typescript is set as a superscript: c^X.
A handwritten mark appears near 'laissons au' in the margin; it is not mathematical.
